question: Can a bounded incremental causal graph-growth algorithm construct unseen two-stage Boolean causal circuits from active interventions, approximate an exhaustive matched-prior program-search baseline at lower inference-development cost, and survive shared-memory capacity competition?
hypothesis: A two-stage six-beam primitive-graph builder will approach exact full-grammar maximum likelihood on newly generated causal circuits with 16 interventions per world, while measuring real wall-clock and program-evaluation cost. Result may be negative; it is not presumed novel or superior to exact MAP.
predecessor_evidence: AAI-05 primary 43604165867 frozen numeric PASS but novelty audit: direct_fit=hard-MAP over predefined 60 rules, full Bayes same prior outperformed. No integration.

inputs.name: seeded, synthetic, multi-stage boolean causal worlds
inputs.source: Pure standard-library SHA256 seeded generator in frozen evaluator source; no personal, private or external data

frozen_design.splits: DEV root XOR, TRANSFER root AND/OR (selector seeded), all input gate pairs/gates unseen; each world independently sampled. No tuning against any scientific seed.
frozen_design.law: Five binary inputs: three state bits and two action bits. Output consists of two bits; each bit is a freshly sampled two-level graph: first gate op_a(pair_a) and second gate op_b(pair_b), root op_r(gate_a,gate_b) then XOR bias. Gates from XOR/AND/OR; pair from ten input-bit pairs, op from three. Symmetric graph aliases accepted, exact MAP applies deterministic lexicographic tie.
frozen_design.observations: Each learner receives 16 distinct do(state,action) observations sampled without replacement from 32 state/action possibilities. Two consequence bits independently flipped with p=.08 per do observation. No passive events accepted as do evidence.
frozen_design.terminal: 12 unseen do decision challenges each with state restricted to states not used in probe training, and random two-bit goal. Choose one of four actions and score 1-Hamming(causal_true_y,goal)/2.
frozen_design.candidate: Two-stage graph construction (no pre-enumerated full program catalog): score all 30 primitive pair/gate nodes under noisy Bernoulli likelihood; take six highest-scoring first nodes per consequence bit; grow second node from all 30 choices with three root operators and two biases; rank completed synthesized graphs on all 16 given observations. Total 1080 completed per bit + 30 unary per bit. Deterministic tie.
controls: Exact exhaustive full-grammar MAP with same 30 primitives and 3 root gates + two biases (5400 complete graphs/bit); same observations and noise
Fully trained conventional 300-epoch logistic (intercept+five singles+ten interactions) on identical do data
Frozen randomized-rule selection from same grammar; no use of observations
Shuffled-label candidate training on negative seeds
Identical learned store class for candidate and exact MAP; value-aware public priority retention and LRU negative control
frozen_design.interference: One real shared two-slot mutable store learns A(public priority=2), B(priority=1), then C(priority=1). With value-aware eviction, A and C must survive; LRU evicts A. Verify original A predictions after both interference updates without restoring any per-world model. Same value-aware policy and memory budget for candidate and exact MAP. This tests storage interference only; priority is hand-given, not learned.
frozen_design.capacity: Per-world two 4-integer circuits (first-primitive,second-primitive,root-op,bias). Shared store exactly two world slots. Candidate beam width six and 1080 completed circuits per output bit; exhaustive 5400. Logistic 16 weights/output, 300 epochs. No hidden training examples.
frozen_design.evaluator: Frozen mean terminal decision reward by cohort, 1024 paired-world bootstrap CI seed 16060, paired differences versus exhaustive MAP and logistic; completed graph evaluations and measured fit/eval wall time, bytes of serialized store and exact online A recall after B,C. No claimed general intelligence or unknown primitive discovery.
frozen_design.data_budget: 32 dev, 64 transfer, 32 negative; 16 do observations and 12 withheld terminal queries per world; separate 32 interference triples; no extra science first use after this primary.
frozen_design.compute_budget: Candidate <=1110 graph/node score candidates per bit per world; exact 5400 completed per bit; logistic 300 epochs; 1024 bootstrap draws per pair. Python 3.12 stdlib and no paid API.

controls: Exact matched-prior exhaustive MAP with identical rule grammar, noise likelihood, action budget and no hidden answers
Fully trained logistic with pair interactions
Random program and shuffled outcome labels
Shared bounded memory store with same value-aware eviction for candidate and exhaustive MAP
metrics: Paired candidate - exhaustive MAP and candidate - logistic reward (paired-world 95% CI)
Training graph-evaluation counts, wall time, cost and serialized inference bytes
Shared store A retention after B,C vs LRU
Determinism excluding wall time; SHA256 prediction receipt

classification_rules.supported: Candidate on TRANSFER within -0.035 of matched exhaustive MAP, candidate versus fully trained logistic >= +0.03, completed graph evaluations <=0.25 of exact, measured fit time candidate/exact <=0.75, shared-store retention 100% for A under public priority and LRU A eviction as negative control, shuffled-label transfer gap >=0.08; score not scientific novelty or native model acceptance.
classification_rules.mixed: Some performance/efficiency positive but at least one prereg gate fails. No promotion.
classification_rules.negative: Sound and reproducible result fails performance, efficiency, shuffle or retention gate. Preserve as negative; never retune used seeds.
classification_rules.invalid: Leakage, protocol/source/seed drift, evaluator implementation error, nonidentifiable generator, logic/cost counter mismatch, or nondeterminism; no claim on result.

prohibited_after_primary_run: retrying consumed primary without a new prereg and disjoint splits
limitations: Grammar still supplies XOR/AND/OR primitives and exact MAP matched vocabulary; online graph growth is structured search, not proof of an unprecedented learning algorithm. The value-aware memory-priority signal is explicitly provided; retention alone does not establish learned salience.
